mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, accompanied by a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), indicates supply-side stress that elevates input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS < previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 1% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to a severe economic shock, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 1% in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 1% combined with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost of capital, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior year for four consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 0% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 6-month averages signals broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month average AND HOUST < 6-month average for the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
